description:
Found by the third cold review of fz-5xp.3. VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING: each repro below
behaves identically at 4f1eefd58 (built in a scratch worktree and compared), so
fz-5xp.3 neither introduced nor worsened any of it. Filed rather than folded in,
because the fix is a closed claim-set that fz-5xp.29/.30 already own the shape of.

fz-5xp.3 made `extern_contract.rs::RUNTIME_SYMBOLS` the authority on how an
fz-owned symbol is called, and refuses a declaration that contradicts it. The
table has 27 rows. The runtime crate exports ~112 `fz_*` symbols, 62 of which
take `*mut Process`. A declaration naming one of the other ~85 gets NO check,
because absence from the table means "fz makes no claim" -- the right default
for `libc::close`, the wrong one for `fz_self_raw`.

THREE REPROS, all from ordinary user code.

  extern "C" fn fz_self_raw() :: integer        # really fn(*mut Process) -> u64
    interp -> misaligned pointer dereference, non-unwinding panic, abort
    run    -> garbage integer
    build  -> a different garbage integer

  extern "C" fn fz_bs_finalize() :: any
    interp -> SIGBUS (exit 138)
    run/build -> refused by cranelift's own signature table

  defmodule Weird do
    extern "C" fn fz_op_add_ii(any, any) :: any # declared C, provided C -- passes
  end                                           # every check, WIRE TYPES differ
    interp -> "invalid any value ref ... UnknownTag(26)"
    run/build -> 5

THREE REASONS IT ESCAPES, each the same shape:

  1. The interpreter's convention gate sits INSIDE the address-book branch
     (`extern_call.rs`), so anything reached by the dlsym fallback is unchecked.
     dlsym does reach the runtime's `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]` exports on macOS.

  2. Whether JIT/AOT refuse is an accident of eager vs lazy declaration.
     `fz_bs_finalize` is pre-declared by `declare_runtime_symbols`, so cranelift
     catches the signature clash; `fz_self_raw` is declared lazily, so nothing
     does. A guard by coincidence, not by construction.

  3. The check compares the ABI but not the WIRE TYPES. `fz_op_add_ii` declared
     `(any, any) :: any` matches on ABI and still diverges, because native
     intercepts the symbol by name and emits arithmetic while interp calls it.

ALSO IN THIS CLASS: the interpreter's `MAX_INTERP_EXTERN_ARGS` ceiling of 4.
A 5-parameter C extern is refused under `interp` and runs under `run`/`build`.
fz-5xp.3 turned that from a `panic!` into a diagnostic, which is why it is not
urgent, but the DIVERGENCE is untouched -- and an `extern "fz"` spends a slot on
the process, so its effective ceiling is 3.

DONE = the claim set is closed. A declaration naming a symbol fz owns must match
the claim in FULL -- ABI, wire types, arity -- or be refused in the shared front
end where every door sees the same answer; and the dlsym fallback must stop being
a hole around the convention gate. That requires knowing what fz owns, which is
exactly the `intrinsic` declaration form fz-5xp.29 and fz-5xp.30 propose: once
intrinsics stop wearing extern syntax, the owned set is enumerable and the
`fz_op_*` shims stop being private interpreter functions masquerading as runtime
exports.

Do this AFTER .29/.30. Doing it first means hand-maintaining an 85-row table,
which is the name-keying fz-5xp.3 exists to delete.

WATCH OUT: no fixture executes a user-declared extern across all three doors --
`grep -rl 'extern "' fixtures2/` finds 20 files, none of them user externs in the
behavior matrix. That is the hole all three of these repros passed through.
title: [BUG] A foreign declaration of an fz-owned symbol is unchecked, and diverges across doors
